objects.derivation: This complete pick-and-place succeeded in every development init, so it is unchanged. The plate top is 0.4557 m, which is 0.4557-0.4393=0.0164 m above its origin. The mug origin is 0.0024 m below its bottom, so its supported origin offset is 0.0164-0.0024=0.0140 m; adding 0.0050 m release clearance gives place_dz=0.0190 m. The 0.003 m tolerance is one tenth of the accepted XY radius of 0.03 m. With lift_dz=0.15, the mug bottom reaches 0.4344+0.15+0.0024=0.5868 m, clearing the tallest non-target top at 0.5694 m by 0.0174 m. At transport_dz=0.15, its bottom is 0.4393+0.15+0.0024=0.5917 m. The compatible registered grasp produced one feasible candidate and consistently completed the grasp.

Placement succeeded whenever this mug was grasped, so its height parameters are retained. The plate top offset is 0.4557-0.4393=0.0164 m. The mug origin is 0.0001 m above its bottom, giving a supported origin offset of 0.0164+0.0001=0.0165 m; adding 0.0050 m release clearance gives place_dz=0.0215 m. The 0.003 m tolerance is safely below the accepted 0.03 m XY radius. Lift places the bottom at 0.4369+0.15-0.0001=0.5868 m, 0.0174 m above the tallest obstacle top; transport places it at 0.4393+0.15-0.0001=0.5892 m. The former registered grasp yielded a repeatedly planner-feasible candidate near yaw 1.8 degrees, lateral -0.0145 m, dz 0.0750 m, and longitudinal 0.0577 m, but three post-close checks detected contact between the gripper hand and this mug's body. The infeasible replacement grid discarded that proven geometry and omitted the approximately 0.0577 m longitudinal handle-side displacement. This candidate restores the proven yaw, lateral, and height while moving 0.0100 m farther outward, to longitudinal 0.0577+0.0100=0.0677 m, reducing palm/body overlap. That position remains within the 0.1 m registry limit and near the mug's longer AABB half-span, 0.1397/2=0.06985 m.

hypothesis: The first predicate and its entire motion were reliable. The failed predicate was white_yellow_mug_1 on plate_2 because execution usually stopped at that mug's post-close grasp guard, not because of transport or placement. The previous 30-candidate grid made matters worse because all candidates lacked the demonstrated handle-side longitudinal displacement and were rejected during approach. I therefore retained the successful order and all validated lift, transport, and placement values, replaced only the second grasp configuration, restored its demonstrated feasible orientation and height, and shifted the hand 10 mm farther outward from the mug body to avoid the observed palm collision while preserving handle reach.
